author: K. D. Lutz
title: Community Care Center of Hondo ranks third largest among Medina County nursing homes in Q1
text:
Community Care Center of Hondo ranked as Medina County’s third largest nursing home in the first quarter of 2026, data from the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) shows .
The facility had 75 beds available, which was 21 fewer than Medina County’s average at that time, and served an average of 46.1 residents during the period.
The CMS awarded Community Care Center of Hondo an overall rating of 1 out of 5, trailing behind the Texas nursing home average rating of 2.7.
During the same quarter, Medina Valley Health & Rehabilitation Center had the highest capacity in Medina County with 116 beds, while Devine Health & Rehabilitation was second with 96 beds available.
Community Care Center of Hondo was fined a total of $18,889 from two penalties as of the first quarter of 2026.
There were three for-profit nursing homes operating in Medina County, Texas, during this period.
U.S. Census Bureau estimates indicate the nation’s older population is increasing as the number of younger residents contracts. Americans age 65 and over grew by 13% between 2020 and 2024, in contrast to a 1.7% decline for those under 18. Over the last century, the older adult demographic in the United States swelled from 4.9 million in 1920 to over 61 million in 2024.
A 2021 analysis estimates nearly half, around 28 million older adults, may someday need long-term services and support, with more than a third expected to require nursing home care at some point.
“Living a long life is something that many of us want and could get,” said Jesse Slome , executive director of the American Association for Long-Term Care Insurance. “But when we live a long life, the chances of us needing long-term care increase exponentially. But when you need that type of care, there are limited options.”
